simple.meaning: בָּתַר (bâthar) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to chop up.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in Genesis, beginning at Genesis 15:10. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to בָּתַר (H1334) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: בָּתַר (bâthar) / H1334 is traced through Genesis 15:10 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H1334. bathar [ בָּתַר ] verb cut in two (Arabic cut off prematurely; extirpate by cutting ) — Qal Perfect בָּתָ֑ר Gen 15:10 ; Pi`el Imperfect וַיְבַתֵּר Gen 15:10 id.
